extractions.description: The paper discusses the inter-dependence between system and data heterogeneity in federated learning (FL) for recommender systems, and its impact on model quality and fairness. It introduces a framework, RF², to model this inter-dependence and evaluates its impact on fairness in FL optimizations. The framework aims to enable more realistic simulations for FL recommender systems, stressing the importance of addressing system-induced data heterogeneity for fair learning outcomes.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily discusses federated learning (FL) in the context of improving fairness and effectiveness of recommender systems. There is no direct focus on any environmental or sustainability issue, which does not fit into the defined eco-responsible AI categories.
primary_category.quote: Federated learning (FL) is an effective mechanism for data privacy in recommender systems by running machine learning model training on-device.

secondary_categories.quote: This paper takes a data-driven approach to show the inter-dependence of data and system heterogeneity in real-world data and quantifies its impact on the overall model quality and fairness.

primary_sub_category.quote: Our evaluation lists several interesting observations. For example, we show that methods that showed similar fairness implications with no system-induced data heterogeneity can show significantly different fairness impacts with realistic system-induced data heterogeneity.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: By analyzing data from a large-scale recommender system deployment, we show that the simplistic assumption is not representative of the real world – in real systems, data and system heterogeneity are tightly intertwined.
